FEDERAL CONSTITUTION

PUBLIC OFFICERS (APPOINTMENT, PROMOTION AND TERMINATION OF SERVICE)

REGULATIONS 2012

IN exercise of the powers conferred by Clause (2) of Article 132 of the Federal

Constitution, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong makes the following regulations:

PART I

PRELIMINARY

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These regulations may be cited as the Public Officers (Appointment,

Promotion and Termination of Service) Regulations 2012.

(2) These Regulations come into operation on 1 January 2012.

Application

2. Subject to the provisions of Part X of the Federal Constitution, these Regulations

shall apply to all appointments, promotions and terminations of service in the public

service.

Application of appointment procedures

3. (1) The procedures specified in these Regulations for making appointments

to a public service under the jurisdiction of a Commission shall apply to all permanent

or temporary appointments except for transfers of appointment, permanent transfers

or any other appointment as decided by the Commission.

(2) For the purpose of this regulation

(a) "transfer of appointment" means an appointment to allow an

officer to transfer to the public services of the Federation, public

service of States, statutory authorities, local authorities or other

scheme of service without being bound by the normal appointment

process pursuant to the dissolution of an agency under any of the

services, scheme of service which has been made obsolete and

abolishment of posts, or on the application of an officer, or on

other grounds as decided by the Government other than

corporatisation or privatisation; and

(b) "permanent transfer" means the permanent appointment of a

serving officer on secondment or temporary transfer to the post

held by him at the agency where he is seconded or temporarily

transfered to.

Interpretation

4. In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires—

"promotion" means substantive upgrading from one grade to a higher grade

within the same service and scheme of service with the approval of the Promotion

Board;

"Head of Department" means an officer who is heading a department or any

officer who is delegated with the powers by the Head of Department in writing to act on

his behalf, and a department includes

(a) a Ministry;

(b) a Federal Department at the federal, regional, state or district level in the

Federation;

(c) a Federal Department abroad; and

(d) any other entity in the public service as determined by the Director

General of Public Service;

"Head of Service" means an officer who is heading a service or any officer

determined by the Director General of Public Service to be a Head of Service;

"lateral appointment" means an appointment to a promotion grade in a scheme

of service;

"Promotion Board" means the Commission, any person or any Promotion Board

as authorized in accordance with the law to promote an officer;

"officer" means all categories of serving officers appointed by the Commission on

permanent, temporary or contract basis;

"appointment" means an appointment to the public service by the Commission

on permanent, temporary or contract basis, including first appointment and

appointment of a serving officer in any scheme of service;

"acting" in relation to an officer, means performing the duties on full time basis

of another post which is of a higher grade than the officer's substantive grade in the

same service and scheme of service, with the approval of the Promotion Board;

"secondment" means the appointment of an officer under

(a) the armed forces;

(b) the judicial and legal service;

(c) the general public service of the Federation;

(d) the police force; or

(e) the education service,

pursuant to Clause (1) of Article 132 of the Federal Constitution to the public service of

States, statutory authorities, local authorities, or any organization in or outside

Malaysia, for a specific period of time without severing the ties of the officer with his

substantive service, including an appointment of an officer under the joint services

mentioned in Article 133 of the Federal Constitution to the service of a statutory

authority, local authority or organization in or outside Malaysia;

"covering" in relation to an officer, means the performing of duties, besides his

own duties for a specified period, of another post which has been approved by the

appropriate authority;

"registered medical practitioner" means a medical practitioner registered under

the Medical Act 1971 [Act 50], whether a government or private medical officer;

"public service" means the public services of the Federation, which are the

judicial and legal service, the general public service of the Federation, the police force

and the education service pursuant to Clause (1) of Article 132 of the Federal

Constitution;

"temporary transfer" means the appointment of an officer to another service

under

(a) the armed forces;

(b) the judicial and legal service;

(c) the general public service of the Federation;

(d) the police force ; or

(e) the education service,

pursuant to Clause (1) of Article 132 of the Federal Constitution or the appointment of

an officer to a post in another scheme of service under the same appointing authority

for a specific period of time without severing the ties of the officer with his substantive

service;

"Commission" means the Public Services Commission, the Judicial and Legal

Service Commission, the Police Force Commission or the Education Service

Commission, as the case may be.

PART II

APPOINTMENT

Appointment according to the scheme of service

5. (1) All appointments to the public service shall be in accordance with the

conditions specified in the scheme of service for the time being in force.

(2) Subject to subregulation (1), if any condition specified in any scheme of

service needs to be amended, the Head of Service shall first obtain the approval of the

Director General of Public Service before the amendment is made.

Appointment of citizens only

6. (1) All candidates for appointments to the public service must be citizens of

Malaysia.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the Yang di-Pertuan Agong may, on

the ground of national interest, allow the appointment of a non-citizen on contract basis

and the provisions in Part X shall apply to such officer.

Reappointment of a person who has resigned

7. A person who has resigned from the public service may be reappointed to the

public service.

Reappointment of a person who has been required to retire

8. (1) Subject to subregulations (2), (3) and (4), a person who has been required

to retire from the public service may be reappointed to the public service.

(2) In this regulation, "has been required to retire" means medically boarded

out, retirement due to appointment in an organisation or retirement due to the decision

of the Government according to the pension laws in force.

(3) A person who has been medically boarded out from the public service

may be reappointed to the public service if he has been confirmed to be medically fit

and capable of performing his duties satisfactorily by a medical panel established on the

request of the Commission.

(4) For the purpose of subregulation (3), the medical panel shall comprise not

less than two registered medical practitioners, one of whom is a specialist in the disease

which the person who has retired suffered from.

Reappointment of a person whose service has been terminated or dismissed

9. A person who has been terminated from public service or dismissed shall not be

reappointed to the public service except with the special permission of the Commission.

Appointment of an officer to another scheme of service

10. An officer may be appointed to a post in another scheme of service if he fulfills

the conditions required by the other scheme of service.

Reversion to previous scheme of service

11. (1) Subject to subregulation (2), an officer who has been confirmed in his

previous scheme of service before being appointed to another scheme of service, may be

allowed by the Commission to revert to his previous scheme of service and grade if

(a) the officer fails to be confirmed in the other scheme of service,

provided that his failure is not due to his unsatisfactory conduct;

or

(b) the officer applied to revert to his previous scheme of service,

provided that he has undergone the minimum probation period

prescribed under the other scheme of service.

(2) The Commission may allow the officer to revert to his previous scheme of

service and grade before being confirmed in the other scheme of service if

(a) there is a vacancy of post in his previous scheme of service;

(b) the approval of the appropriate Head of Service is obtained; and

(c) the post in the previous scheme of service is under the jurisdiction

of the same appointing authority.

(3) For the purpose of subregulation (1), the officer shall, on the date of his

reinstatement to the previous scheme of service, be given the salary point or salary

amount that the officer should have received if he was not appointed to the current

post, subject to the maximum salary scale in his previous post. The date of the annual

salary movement of the officer is based on the date of the annual salary movement in

the previous scheme of service.

Secondment of an officer

12. (1) An officer appointed on a permanent basis may, with his consent, the

consent of his Head of Department and with the approval of the Commission, be

seconded, subject to such conditions and for such term as may be determined by the

Yang di-Pertuan Agong, to any public service of a State, statutory authority, local

authority or any organization, in or outside Malaysia.

(2) The Commission may consider an officer of a public service of a State

service to be seconded to the public service subject to such conditions and for such term

as may be determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

(3) A statutory authority or local authority may consider an officer of the

statutory authority or local authority to be seconded to the public service, subject to

the consent of the officer, such statutory authority or local authority and the party to

whom the officer is seconded to and any conditions and for such term as agreed by

the parties involved.

Temporary transfer

13. An officer who is appointed on a permanent basis may, with the approval of the

Commission, be appointed on temporary transfer to any post in the public service,

subject to such conditions and for such term as may be determined by the Director

General of Public Service.

PART III

RECRUITMENT

Recruitment procedure

14. (1) Any recruitment to a public service shall be advertised in at least one

daily Malay language newspaper.

(2) For the purpose of subregulation (1), the advertisement shall state,

among other things

(a) the title of the post and the status of appointment;

(b) the name of the scheme of service;

(c) particulars of the salary;

(d) the required academic and other qualifications;

(e) the citizenship's status of the applicant;

(f) the closing date for applications; and

(g) the address to which applications should be sent.

(3) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the Commission may use any other

method as it thinks suitable to advertise the recruitment.

Vetting procedure

15. The Commision may implement vetting procedure according to profile or other

suitable vetting procedures for the purpose of getting the best candidate to be

appointed to the public service.

Particulars of recruitment

16. (1) The Head of Service shall inform the Commission of any required

particulars in every recruitment exercise as follows:

(a) the number of vacant posts which need to be filled up;

(b) the number of reserved candidates required;

(c) special conditions, if any; and

(d) the description of the duties and responsibilities of the vacant post.

(2) If the qualifications or conditions in the scheme of service for the vacant

post need to be amended for the recruitment exercise, the Head of Service shall first

obtain the approval of the Director General of Public Service before informing the

Commission as required by subregulation (1).

Equivalent qualification

17. Where any doubt arises in any scheme of service or advertisement of any

vacancies regarding the meaning of qualification which is recognized as equivalent in

the required field of the scheme of service, the matter shall be referred to the Director

General of Public Service for determination.

Application from an officer

18. An application from a serving officer shall be submitted to the Commission and

notified to the Head of Department, and the Commission may acquire the comments of

the Head of Department if necessary.

Offer of appointment by the Commission

19. (1) The Commission shall make an offer of appointment to successful

candidates either directly or through the Head of Service or the Head of Department by

any suitable means as the Commission thinks fit. The Commission shall also inform the

unsuccessful candidates.

(2) The Commission may direct the Head of Service or Head of Department to

make an offer of appointment to the successful candidates on its behalf, and the Head of

Service or the Head of Department who has been so directed shall send to the

Commission a copy of the offer letter for appointment issued by the Head of Service or

the Head of Department.

(3) Every offer letter for appointment shall set out the information on the

service specified by the Commission.

Health examination, statutory declaration and letter of undertaking

20. (1) Every candidate who is to be appointed to the public service shall comply

with the following conditions for appointment:

(a) the candidate shall be examined and certified to be fit to serve by a

registered medical practitioner; and

(b) the candidate shall make a statutory declaration under the

Statutory Declarations Act 1960 [Act 13] that he—

(i) does not have any criminal record;

(ii) has never been dismissed;

(iii) is not a drug addict;

(iv) does not possess foreign citizenship;

(v) is not a bankrupt;

(vi) was not medically boarded out; and

(vii) has never been terminated from public service.

(2) The Commission may determine any other declarations apart from the

declarations prescribed in paragraph (1)(b), if necessary.

(3) Every candidate shall sign the Letter of Undertaking as specified in the

First Schedule that he shall comply with the provisions of the Public Officers (Conduct

and Discipline) Regulations 1993 [P. U. (A) 395/1993], General Orders, circulars, circular

letters, regulations and other orders issued by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong from time to

time throughout his service in the public service.

(4) An officer who has complied with the conditions of subregulation (1) may

be required to comply with those conditions again when appointed to another scheme

of service.

(5) The Commission may revoke the offer of appointment if the candidate is

found to be unfit after being examined in accordance with paragraph (1)(a) or does not

comply with any of the conditions mentioned in paragraph (1)(b) and subregulation (3).

(6) For the purpose of subregulation (5), any candidate who has already

commenced service may be paid any emolument for the period of his service before the

offer for service is revoked.

(7) For the purpose of appointments of candidates under subregulation 6(2),

the conditions under subparagraphs (1)(b)(iv) and (vii) are not applicable to the

candidate.

(8) Notwithstanding paragraph 1(a), the Head of Department may direct a

serving officer to undergo medical examination or to submit medical report certified by

a registered medical practitioner if the Head of Department is of the opinion that it is

necessary for the service.

Security vetting

21. An officer who is appointed for the first time or an officer who is appointed to

another scheme of service is required to pass the security vetting as prescribed if it is so

stipulated in any laws in force.

Acknowledgement of acceptance

22. The Head of Department shall send to the Commission the acknowledgement of

acceptance of the offer of appointment from the candidate, together with the

certification by the registered medical practitioner, the statutory declaration and the

Letter of Undertaking required under subregulations 20(1) and (3) and shall inform the

Commission the date the candidate reports for duty.

PART IV

DATE OF APPOINTMENT, INITIAL SALARY AND ANNUAL SALARY MOVEMENT

Date of appointment

23. (1) The date of appointment of an officer to the public service is the date he

reports for duty, unless otherwise determined by the Commission.

(2) The Head of Service or the Head of Department shall not accept any

officer who reports for duty if the officer has not complied with the conditions for

appointment in subregulation 20(1).

(3) For the purpose of subregulation (2), the officer is still subject to the

maximum period to report for duty as prescribed by the Commission in the offer letter

for appointment.

Date of permanent appointment for a temporary officer

24. Where a temporary officer who complies with all the conditions specified for any

scheme of service is appointed to fill any vacant permanent post in such scheme of

service, the date of appointment of the officer to that permanent post shall be the date

the Commission meets and approves the permanent appointment.

Determination of initial salary

25. (1) The Commission shall determine the initial salary of an officer as

prescribed in the scheme of service.

(2) If an officer who is to be appointed for the first time possesses working

experience which is relevant to the post he is going to hold, he may be granted a higher

initial salary.

(3) If the Commission is considering a higher initial salary under

subregulation (2), the determination of the higher salary shall be based on one normal

salary movement for every complete year of the relevant working experience, limited to

the maximum salary of the grade for the post.

(4) Notwithstanding subregulation (3), the Commission has the discretion to

determine a part of or the total number of years of the relevant working experience to

be taken into consideration in determining the higher initial salary.

(5) The working experience which is considered as relevant to an officer in

the Managerial and Professional Group is the working experience obtained after the

officer has acquired his professional or academic qualifications as determined in the

appropriate scheme of service.

(6) Subregulations (2), (3) and (4) shall also apply

(a) in determining the initial salary of an unconfirmed officer who is

subsequently appointed to another scheme of service; and

(b) in determining the initial salary of an officer who is reappointed in

accordance with regulations 7, 8 and 9.

(7) If an officer who has been confirmed in service is subsequently appointed

to another scheme of service, the initial salary of the officer shall be at a higher salary

point and nearest in which the difference shall not be less than one normal salary

movement or of the same amount with the normal salary movement in the previous

grade or post, limited to the maximum salary point of the new post.

(8) If an officer who has been confirmed in service is appointed to another

post on the same or earlier date of his salary movement in his previous post, the salary

movement in his previous post, if any, shall first be given, limited to the maximum

amount of the salary of the said grade, before determining the initial salary of the

appointment.

(9) The initial salary of an officer who is appointed for the first time by way of

lateral appointment is based on the minimum salary point of the post.

(10) The initial salary of an officer who has not been confirmed in the service

in which he is appointed by way of lateral appointment is as specified in

subregulation (9).

(11) The initial salary of an officer who has been confirmed in service and

subsequently appointed by way of lateral appointment is as specified in

subregulation (7).

Initial salary in special cases

26. Notwithstanding regulation 25, the Commission may determine that the initial

salary of an officer is at any salary point or a particular salary amount for a particular

post after taking into consideration

(a) the special qualification or talent of the officer; or

(b) the special circumstances as determined by the Government in relation to

the appointment of the officer.

Annual salary movement

27. (1) The date of the annual salary movement of permanent and temporary

officers shall be as set out in the Second Schedule.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the Director General of Public

Service may, in certain conditions, determine the date of salary movement of an

officer on a date which he thinks fit.

(3) The date of the annual salary movement of an officer who is on

secondment or temporary transfer shall be as determined by the Commission.

(4) The annual salary movement of an officer shall be based on the annual

work performance of the officer or such other conditions as determined by the Yang

di-Pertuan Agong from time to time.

PART V

PROBATION PERIOD, CONFIRMATION OF SERVICE

AND EXTENSION OF PROBATION PERIOD

Probation period

28. (1) Every officer appointed is required to serve on probation for a period of

six to twenty-four months.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the Commission may, in special

circumstances, shorten the probation period of an officer or exempt an officer from

probation period.

Conditions for confirmation

29. (1) An officer on probation who has fulfilled all the conditions specified in the

scheme of service or such other conditions as determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong

from time to time is eligible for confirmation in service by the Commission.

(2) The Head of Department shall submit to the Commission the form set out

in the Third Schedule, either to certify or not to certify the confirmation of the officer.

(3) If an officer is certified to be confirmed in service, the Head of Department

shall submit a certification in the form set out in the Third Schedule within one month

from the date the officer is eligible to be certified for confirmation, provided that the

certification is submitted in not less than the minimum probation period.

(4) If an officer is not certified to be confirmed in service, the Head of

Department shall submit to the Commission a certification not to confirm the officer in

service as set out in the Third Schedule.

(5) If the Head of Department fails to submit the certification for the

confirmation of an officer in accordance with subregulation (3), the officer may apply to

the Commission to be confirmed and a copy of the application shall be sent to the Head

of Department.

(6) After receiving the application under subregulation (5), the Commission

may conduct an investigation and upon completion of the investigation confirms the

officer if the Commission finds him to be eligible for confirmation.

(7) Notwithstanding subregulation (2), the Commission is not bound by the

certification of a Head of Department in confirming an officer in service.

(8) If there is any condition for confirmation in service which needs to be

amended in special circumstances, the Head of Service shall first obtain the approval of

Commission.

Extension of probation period

30. (1) The Commission may extend the probation period of an officer, whether

with or without penalty, after undergoing the maximum probation period prescribed in

the scheme of service.

(2) If an officer has not fulfilled the conditions to be confirmed in service after

undergoing the prescribed maximum probation period, the officer may submit an

application for the extension of his probation period to the Commission through his

Head of Department immediately after the expiry of his maximum probation period,

provided that the Head of Department has not submitted the certification not to confirm

the officer in service under subregulation 29(4).

(3) If the Head of Department agrees to certify the application of the officer,

the Head of Department shall immediately submit the the form as set out in the Forth

Schedule in accordance with subregulation (2) to the Commission stating the following

particulars:

(a) the reasons for not confirming the officer;

(b) the recommendation of the Head of Department on whether the

probation period should be extended, with or without penalty;

(c) the up-dated particulars of service of the officer; and

(d) the list of examinations, if any, that the officer has sat for, the dates

and results of the examinations.

(4) The Commission shall only approve the application for an extension of the

probation which is submitted in accordance with subregulation (3) if there are

reasonable grounds for believing that the officer is able to comply with the conditions

for his confirmation during the extended period applied for and the Head of Department

recommends that the probation period of the officer be extended.

(5) The probation period of an officer may only be extended for not more

than twelve months, but the Commission may in special circumstances extend the

probation period for more than twelve months if it thinks fit.

(6) Any decision made by the Commission in respect of an application for the

extension of the probation period of an officer shall be conveyed to the officer by the

Commission within a period of one month from the date of the decision.

Date of confirmation

31. (1) The date of confirmation in service of a officer is the first day after the

date the officer has complied with all the conditions prescribed for confirmation.

(2) An officer shall be deemed to be on probation until the officer is

confirmed in service by the Commission, even if the officer has already complied with all

the conditions prescribed for confirmation.

Effect of extension of probation period with penalty

32. An officer whose probation period is extended with penalty shall

(a) lose his seniority for a period equal to the extended period;

(b) not be eligible for any annual salary movement during the extended

period; and

(c) subject to the date of his confirmation, the date of his annual salary

movement be changed to the following year.

Notification of confirmation

33. The Commission shall immediately notify an officer of his confirmation in service

through the Head of Department of the officer.

PART VI

SENIORITY

Method of determining seniority

34. (1) The seniority of an officer is determined as follows:

(a) for an officer on an appointment grade or lateral appointment

grade, according to the date the officer was appointed

permanently; and

(b) for an officer on a promotional grade, according to the date the

officer holds the grade substantively.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), where two or more officers are

appointed permanently or promoted to the same grade in the same scheme of service

on the same date, the seniority of the officers are deemed to be equal.

Seniority of an officer who reverts to his previous scheme of service

35. An officer who reverts to his previous scheme of service in accordance with

subregulation 11(1) loses his seniority for the period the officer remains outside his

previous scheme of service.

Seniority of an officer who is granted leave without pay and absent from duty

36. (1) An officer will lose his seniority in the following circumstances:

(a) granted unpaid leave, other than unpaid study leave for the period

he is on such leave; or

(b) absent from duty without leave, permission or reasonable excuse

for the period of his absence.

(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1)(b), the power of the disciplinary authority

to impose any disciplinary action against an officer who is found to be absent from duty

without leave, without approval or any other reasonable grounds is not affected.

PART VII

OPTION FOR EMPLOYEES PROVIDENT FUND SCHEME AND CONFERMENT

OF PENSIONABLE STATUS

Option for Employees Provident Fund Scheme

37. (1) An officer who wishes to opt for the Employees Provident Fund Scheme

as provided under section 6A of the Pensions Act 1980 [Act 227] or pension laws for the

time being in force shall, before being confirmed in service, exercise his option by using

the form set out in the Fifth Schedule.

(2) An officer who has opted for Employees Provident Fund Scheme in his

previous post and appointed to another post in the public service, public service of a

State, statutory authority or local authority shall be subject to subregulation (1).

Conferment of pensionable status

38. (1) An officer who has not opted for the Employees Provident Fund Scheme

in accordance with regulation 37 is eligible to be conferred with pensionable status in

accordance with the pensions laws.

(2) When an officer becomes eligible to be conferred with pensionable status,

the Head of Department of the officer shall submit his certification in the form set out in

the Sixth Schedule to the Commission.

(3) The appointment of an officer to another permanent post in the public

service in accordance with regulation 10 shall not affect the pensionable status in

accordance with the pensions laws, except if the officer opted for the Employees

Provident Fund Scheme when appointed to the other post.

PART VIII

PROMOTION, ACTING AND COVERING

The basis for promotion

39. (1) The promotion of an officer is based on merit.

(2) In considering the merit of an officer for promotion, the Promotion Board

shall take into consideration

(a) the efficiency and performance of the work of the officer;

(b) the qualifications, knowledge, skills and experience of the officer;

(c) the personal characteristics, including his suitability for the

promotional post, integrity, potential and leadership of the officer;

and

(d) the extramural activities and contributions of the officer to the

country and society.

(3) In addition to the matters specified in subregulation (2), the Promotion

Board may consider any other aspects which it thinks relevant.

(4) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), if two or more officers are adjudged

equal in terms of merit, the academic qualifications or working experience related to the

promotional post, as well as the seniority of the officers, shall also be made a basis for

selection and consideration.

Conditions for promotion

40. (1) Notwithstanding regulation 39, an officer may only be considered for

promotion if the officer has complied with all the conditions specified in his scheme of

service and if there is a vacancy in the promotional post, unless the scheme of service

provides otherwise.

(2) The Director General of Public Service in special circumstances may

exempt certain conditions of the scheme of service for the purpose of promotion of an

officer under subregulation (1).

Promotion of an officer on secondment or temporary transfer

41. Where an officer is on secondment in accordance with subregulation 12(1) or

temporary transfer in accordance with regulation 13 has complied with all the

conditions for promotion, the officer shall be considered in any promotion exercise

conducted in relation to his substantive scheme of service.

Advertisement of a vacancy of a promotional post

42. (1) If the Promotion Board is of the opinion that a vacancy of a promotional

post is to be filled by inviting eligible applicants from a particular service under a

particular department only, the Head of Department shall advertise the vacancy through

a departmental circular or other suitable means.

(2) If there is a vacancy of a promotional post which does not require an

advertisement, the Head of Department shall make a certification to the appropriate

Promotion Board to fill the vacancy by certifying eligible officers, according to the

scheme of service, for consideration.

(3) For the purpose of subregulation (2), the Head of Department may certify

to the Promotion Board any additional conditions to be imposed so as to obtain a more

reasonable number of suitably qualified officers.

Date of promotion

43. (1) Subject to subregulations (2) and (3), the date of promotion of an officer

is the date determined by the Promotion Board.

(2) For promotion to a grade, the date shall not be earlier than the date of

vacancy of the post or the date the respective officer is eligible to be promoted

according to his scheme of service, whichever is the later, but the date shall not be

earlier than the last promotion date for the same grade in a previous exercise.

(3) For promotion to a post, except if the scheme of service does not stipulate

that a promotion is subject to a vacancy of the post, the date of promotion shall not be

earlier than the date the officer is approved to act in the post or on the date the

substantive post becomes vacant, whichever is the later.

(4) For the purpose of this regulation

(a) "promotion to a grade" is a promotion to any grade in the

Managerial and Professional Group and the Implementer Group;

and

(b) "promotion to a post" is a promotion to any post in the Top

Management Group.

Determination of promotional salary

44. (1) Subject to subregulation (3), the salary received by an officer who has

been promoted shall be higher than the last-drawn salary received in the previous

grade.

(2) For the purpose of subregulation (1)

(a) if the last-drawn salary in the previous grade is less than the

minimum salary in the promotional grade, and the difference is

equal to or more than one normal salary movement or an amount

which is equal to one normal salary movement in the previous

grade or post, the officer shall be paid the minimum salary in the

promotional grade;

(b) if the last-drawn salary in the previous grade is less than the

minimum salary in the promotional grade but the difference is less

than one normal salary movement or an amount which is equal to

one normal salary movement in the previous grade or post, the

initial salary shall be determined at a salary point or salary amount

of the promotional grade subsequent to the minimum salary point

such that the difference between his last-drawn salary in the

previous grade and his new salary in the promotional grade is

equal to or more than one normal salary movement or salary

amount which is equal to one normal salary movement in his

previous grade; and

(c) if the last-drawn salary in the previous grade is equal to or higher

than the minimum salary in the promotional grade, the officer shall

be paid a salary at a higher salary point nearest to his last-drawn

salary in the previous grade and the difference between the salary

in the promotional grade and the salary in the previous grade shall

be not less than one normal salary movement or an amount which

is equal to one normal salary movement in the previous grade or

post.

(3) Where an officer is promoted earlier or on the same date as the date of his

salary movement in his previous post, the salary movement in his previous post, if any,

shall be given first before determining the initial salary in the promotional post.

Date of salary movement in the promotional post

45. The date of the annual salary movement of an officer who is promoted shall be

determined in accordance with the date on which his promotion comes into force

according to subregulation 27(1).

Acting and covering

46. An officer may, whenever required in the interest of the service and subject to

the approval of the appropriate authority, be directed to act or to cover the duties of

another post.

Acting and covering allowances

47. An officer who has been approved to act or to cover the duties of another post is

eligible to be paid acting or covering allowance in accordance with the regulations for

the time being in force.

PART IX

TERMINATION OF SERVICE AND RESIGNATION

Termination of service of an unconfirmed officer

48. (1) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may terminate the service of an officer who

has not been confirmed in service if the officer has

(a) concealed any information regarding his health in the medical

examination form;

(b) made false declaration in the statutory declaration as required by

paragraph 20(1)(b) and subregulation 20(2);

(c) failed to comply with the requirement in subregulation 20(3); or

(d) amended or falsified any document relating to his appointment.

(2) For the purpose of terminating the service of an officer under

paragraph (1)(a), the Head of Department may direct the officer to undergo medical

examination again or the Head of Department may acquire the health information of the

officer by any suitable means.

Termination of service of an officer who fails the security vetting

49. (1) The service of an officer who fails the security vetting during the

probation period or extended probation period may be terminated.

(2) The service of an officer who fails the security vetting after being

confirmed in service may be terminated in accordance with the Public Officers

(Disciplinary and Conduct) Regulations 1993.

Termination of service of an officer who fails to be confirmed

50. (1) Subject to subregulation (2), the Yang di-Pertuan Agong may terminate

the service of an officer who is on probation for his first appointment who has failed to

be confirmed in service during the probation period, whether the initial probation

period or its extention.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the service of an officer may be

terminated if he fails in a course or training which is a condition for the purpose of

confirmation in service.

(3) An officer who has been confirmed in service in the previous scheme of

service and is subsequently appointed to a new scheme of service but fails to be

confirmed may be terminated under subregulation (4). Termination under this

provision is deemed to be a termination in the public interest and any pension matters

resulting from the termination shall be subject to the pensions laws in force.

(4) For the purpose of subregulation (5), representations shall be made by

the Head of Department to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to terminate the service of an

officer in the public interest by submitting a full report stating where the officer is

serving or has served.

(5) The report mentioned in subregulation (4) shall contain the particulars

relating to the service of the officer and comments of the Head of Department, if any.

(6) If, after considering the report received under subregulation (5), the Yang

di-Pertuan Agong is satisfied that, having regard to the conditions of service and the

usefulness of the officer to the service, it is desirable in the public interest to do so, the

Yang di-Pertuan Agong may terminate the service of the officer from the date as shall be

determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

(7) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in these Regulations and any

other law, in terminating the service of any officer in the public interest under this

regulation, such officer may not be given any opportunity to be heard according to

Clause (2) of Article 135 of the Federal Constitution.

(8) For the purpose of this regulation, the service of an officer, other than

those mentioned in subregulations (1) and (2), shall be terminated if the officer is not

able to revert to his previous scheme of service according to paragraph 11(1)(a).

(9) For the purpose of subregulation (1), "first appointment" means the first

appointment to the public service or the reappointment of an officer in accordance with

regulations 7, 8 and 9.

Authority to terminate service

51. The authority which may terminate the service of an officer under

regulations 48, 49 and 50 shall not be lower than the appointing authority or the board

of officers which has been delegated with the authority by the Commission under

Clause (6) of Article 144 of the Federal Constitution.

Opportunity to show cause

52. The service of an officer shall not be terminated under regulations 48 and 49 and

subregulations 50(1) and (2) unless the officer has been given the opportunity to show

cause, within a period of not less than fourteen days from the date of receipt of notice to

show cause, as to why his service shall not be terminated.

Notice of termination of service

53. (1) The Yang di-Pertuan Agong may terminate the service of an officer after

giving him a written notice or one month salary in lieu of the notice if

(a) the officer has not responded to the notice to show cause under

regulation 52 within the specified period; and

(b) the Yang di-Pertuan Agong is satisfied that no reasonable ground

exists for not terminating the service of the officer.

(2) For the purposes of regulations 48, 49 and 50, the period of the written

notice specified in subregulation (1) is thirty days.

(3) Notwithstanding subregulation (2), for an officer who is appointed other

than to a permanent appointment, the period of the written notice shall be

(a) according to the terms of appointment of the officer; or

(b) if the period is not provided in the terms of his appointment, thirty

days.

Notice of resignation

54. (1) Subject to regulation 56, an officer who wishes to resign shall submit a

written notice

(a) for an officer who is appointed on a permanent basis, thirty days

before the resignation takes effect or one month salary in lieu of

notice; and

(b) for an officer who is appointed on other than permanent basis,

according to the terms of appointment of the officer or if the

period is not provided in the terms of his appointment, thirty days

before the resignation takes effect or one month salary in lieu of

notice.

(2) The notice of resignation shall be sent by the officer to the Head of

Department and the Head of Department shall issue a written acknowledgement of

receipt to the officer and provide a copy to the Head of Service when the notice of

resignation is received.

(3) The Head of Department shall record the resignation of the officer in the

record of service of the officer.

The coming into effect of resignation notice

55. (1) Every resignation shall take effect on the day following the day on which

the period of notice given by the officer expires.

(2) The resignation which has come into effect shall not be withdrawn.

The shortening of resignation notice

56. The Head of Department may allow the period of the resignation notice of any

officer to be shortened on any of the following grounds:

(a) the officer is offered to hold any post in a public service of a State,

statutory authority, local authority or a company in which the

Government has an interest;

(b) the officer or his spouse, child or parent of the officer is suffering from

health problems;

(c) the officer is attending a course or training; or

(d) any other grounds approved by the Director General of the Public Service.

Resignation is not required

57. An officer who was appointed on a permanent or temporary basis and who is

appointed to another service in the public service, is not required to resign, provided

that he shall inform the Head of Department in writing to release the post.

PART X

APPOINTMENT OF A CONTRACT OFFICER

Appointment of a contract officer

58. (1) Notwithstanding Part II, the Commission may appoint an officer on a

contract basis.

(2) The policy and procedure for the appointment of an officer on contract

shall be determined by the Director General of Public Service.

Termination of service and resignation of a contract officer

59. Subregulation 53(3) and paragraph 54(1)(b) shall apply to the termination of

service and resignation of a contract officer.

PART XI

AGE

Age and date of birth

60. (1) Where a scheme of service specifies an age requirement, then the age

referred to is the age according to the Gregorian calendar.

(2) For the purpose of subregulation (1), the age of a person is determined in

accordance with the following provisions:

(a) if the actual date of birth is known, the age shall be according to

that date;

(b) if only the month is known, the last day of the month shall be

deemed to be the date of birth;

(c) if only the year is known, 31 December of that year shall be

deemed to be the date of birth;

(d) if the date of birth is 29 February, then the birthday anniversary of

the person for the year which does not have the date 29 February

shall be deemed to be 1 March.

Retirement age

61. The retirement age of an officer is as determined by the pensions laws.

PART XII

MISCELLANEOUS

Powers of the Director General of Public Service

62. (1) Except for the power which has been delegated to him, the Director

General of Public Service may, from time to time, in writing, delegate his power under

these Regulations to any officer.

(2) The Director General of Public Service may, from time to time, if

necessary, issue guidelines to clarify any provision in these Regulations.

Savings and transitional

63. (1) Nothing in these Regulations shall affect the validity and operation of any

decision made in respect of any matter under previous General Orders and regulations,

and such decision shall continue to have full force and effect notwithstanding anything

inconsistent with or contrary to any provision in these Regulations.

(2) All matters and proceedings which were pending before any Commission

prior to the commencement of these Regulations shall continue to be dealt with in

accordance with the Public Officer (Appointment, Promotion and Termination) 2005

[P.U. (A) 176/2005] as if those Regulations had not been repealed.

(3) Any guidelines issued prior to the coming into operation of these

Regulations shall continue to be applicable in so far as it is not contrary to any of the

provisions in these Regulations.

(4) An officer on probation may be confirmed on or after the date of coming

into operation of these Regulations, subject to the officer having been in service for a

probation period of six months or more and fulfilling all conditions for confirmation

other that the condition on probation period prescribed under the scheme of service

before these Regulations come into operation.

(5) An officer on probation who has served for twenty-four months or more

but has not been confirmed in service on the date these Regulations come into

operation is allowed to complete the balance of his initial probation period under the

scheme of service before these Regulations come into operation or the balance of the

probation period which is extended by the Commission and the officer may be

confirmed if he has fulfilled all the conditions for confirmation as prescribed under the

scheme of service.

Revocation

64. (1) The Public Officers (Appointment, Promotion and Termination Of Service)

Regulations 2005 are revoked except for subregulations 26(1) and 28(6) for the officers

who are in the Malaysian Remuneration System.

(2) Notwithstanding subregulation (1), the General Orders 45 and 49 of the

General Orders Chapter A (Appointments and Promotion) 1973 shall continue to be

applicable to the officers who are in the Special Cabinet Committee 1976 Remuneration

System.
